task_language: stack the left bowl on the right bowl and place them in the tray

subtasks.name: pick(left_bowl)
subtasks.outcome: never attempted: pi0 picked the right bowl (the base) instead

subtasks.name: place(stacked_bowls, tray, in)
subtasks.outcome: partial: the right (base) bowl alone was placed in the tray

behaviour_summary: pi0 grasped the robot's-right bowl (image left, nearest the tray), carried it straight into the tray by ~step 160, then hovered over the tray until timeout; the left bowl never moved.

failures.mode_definition: In a multi-step instruction, pi0 skips an intermediate subtask (e.g. stacking one object on another) and carries a single object straight to the final destination, then never completes the remaining steps.
hl_remedy: HALT once a single bowl is carried toward the tray before the stack VERIFY passes
if the base (right) bowl already sits in the tray: REPROMPT 'pick up the left bowl and place it on the right bowl'
otherwise RETREAT up 10 cm and REPROMPT 'pick up the left bowl and place it on the right bowl'
VERIFY left bowl rests in right bowl
if the stack is not yet in the tray: REPROMPT 'pick up the right bowl and place it in the tray'
WATCH 5 s; retry once, then ESCALATE
failures.prevention: Coordinator issues the stack and the place as two separate prompts and advances only after a VERIFY that the top bowl rests inside the base bowl.
failures.observation: Step 40 gripper descends on the image-left bowl (= robot's right, the stacking base); 60-80 that bowl is grasped and lifted; 100-140 carried left and lowered into the tray; 160-409 bowl in tray, gripper hovering/still above it. Image-right (left) bowl never touched.

notes: Two errors in one decision: wrong bowl chosen first (base instead of top) and the stack step skipped; recorded as one HL failure. After the placement pi0 idles over the tray (HL-1-like) rather than fetching the second bowl; treated as a consequence of the collapsed plan. Since the base bowl is already in the tray, stacking the left bowl onto it in place would plausibly satisfy the goal.
